title: Detection of finite signed tensor maps on coherent frames
statement: For a finite purity setting P [def-pur-conventions], a k-scheme T, and integers r,t,s, use its fixed-scalar signed coefficient sheaves [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data]. A coherent frame consists of bases of all intrinsic signed lines, with coefficient one at zero, ordered positive tensor powers, and evaluation-dual negative bases [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. The ordinary-section realization is the scalar realization unit followed by its counit. If two morphisms from F_r tensor F_t to F_s have equal realized values on the pure tensors of every pair of ordinary representatives of every coherent frame basis in degrees r,t, then the two morphisms are equal. Neither morphism is assumed invertible or normalized to the degree-s basis.

source.place: Step 2: compatibility with the invertible twist by associativity; expanded local coherent-frame construction of signed products. Stacks sites-modules.tex, section-tensor-product and section-invertible.

proof.text: Trivialize the first line on a covering sieve using its finite locally free rank-one theorem. On each chart and further restriction construct the coefficient-unit, ordered-power and evaluation-dual bases; these satisfy all coherent frame equations.

The scalar realization unit is a bijection on sections since its underlying additive sheafification unit is invertible on a sheaf. The counit is a sectionwise isomorphism. Thus each frame basis has ordinary representatives. The intrinsic tensor comparison identifies their product with the basis of the tensor line.

The hypothesis gives equality on these generators. Intrinsic module linearity gives equality on all local multiples; sheafification locally represents tensor sections by finite sums of pure tensors. Target separatedness descends equality from the covering sieve. Faithfulness of realization gives equality of fixed-scalar sheaf morphisms. Zero degrees, opposite signs, zero rings and empty objects use the same universal properties.

mathlib_searches.query: A sheaf morphism of invertible modules sending local basis generators to basis generators is an isomorphism and is uniquely determined
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results, including Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso, GrothendieckTopology.W_sheafToPreheaf_map_iff_isIso and PresheafOfModules.homEquivOfIsLocallyBijective. They provide general sheaf tools, but none supplies coherent signed frame products for these finite fixed-scalar lines.

mathlib_searches.query: Tensor product of signed integer powers of an invertible sheaf with local basis normalization
mathlib_searches.results: Eight results, including CommRing.Pic.mk_tensor and CommRing.Pic.mul_eq_tensor, concern classes of modules or unrelated scheme sections; none is a normalized sheaf product map or its frame detection criterion. Loogle query "tensorPow", "add" had zero hits.

Mathlib search returned numerical zpow identities, no sheaf product. Read NormalizedSignedTensorPowers (categorical products but no coherent-frame normalization), SignedLineOrdinaryConstraints (successive positive powers and evaluation), and FinitePositiveChartFrameExt (positive single-line detection requiring a first chart; imports the item). Blueprint searches "signed tensor" returned four unrelated operation definitions; "coherent frame" returned no node. No duplicate of the three local sheaf steps.

theorem finiteTensorSheafProduct_frame_ext (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [T.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] (r t s : ℤ)
    (f g : P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T r ⊗ P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T t ⟶
      P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T s)
    (h : ∀ (V : T.ProEt) (e : P.FiniteTensorFrame T V)
      (x : (P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T r).obj.obj (Opposite.op V))
      (y : (P.finiteTensorFixedSheaf T t).obj.obj (Opposite.op V)),
      P.finiteTensorSection T r V x = e.basis r 0 →
      P.finiteTensorSection T t V y = e.basis t 0 →
      P.finiteTensorSection T s V
        (f.hom.app (Opposite.op V) (P.finiteTensorSectionTmul T r t V x y)) =
      P.finiteTensorSection T s V
        (g.hom.app (Opposite.op V) (P.finiteTensorSectionTmul T r t V x y))) :
    f = g
